title: Resume details
description: Your resume facts. CEZ Job Finder reads this file every time it makes a resume for you.

month.description: Year then month, like 2023-02 for February 2023. A year alone, like 2023, when you only know the year - the page then shows years only.

bullets.description: One thing you did, per line. Keep each to a single sentence.

contact.description: Your name and how an employer reaches you.

name.description: The name that goes at the top of the page.

location.description: Town and state, like Springfield, IL.

links.description: LinkedIn, a portfolio, anything worth a click.

legal_first.description: First name as on your ID. Only for application boxes that ask for your legal name - never printed on the page. Give it with legal_last, or leave both out.

legal_middle.description: Middle name as on your ID, if you have one. Optional.

legal_last.description: Last name as on your ID. Give it with legal_first, or leave both out.

other_names.description: Names you used before, like a maiden name or another spelling. Only for application boxes asking for other names, like a background check.

form_name.description: Which name goes in a plain Name box on applications when it differs from the top of your page: legal, or page for the name at the top of your resume.

form_jobs.description: Which jobs go in an application's work history when your tailored resume left the oldest off: page for the same jobs as the resume, all for every job. A form asking for your complete work history always gets all.

headline.description: One line above your summary saying what you do - your real title and main skills, like Software Engineer | React.js, TypeScript, Node.js. Leave it out if you prefer none.

summary.description: The short pitch at the top of the page - up to four lines.

education_first.description: true puts Education above your jobs, false below them. Leave it out and Job Finder follows the usual convention: Education first while you're a student or just graduated, after your jobs once you've worked a few years.

roles.description: Your jobs, newest first. Leave it as [] if you have not had one yet.

company.description: The employer's name, written the way they write it.

title.description: Your job title, spelled out - Senior, not Sr.

blurb.description: One line on what the employer does, if it is not obvious.

oneOf.description: The job you are in now.

ai_era.description: Set this only to overrule the dates about whether AI work belongs in this job.

career_break.description: Time away from work, said plainly. Shown with your jobs in date order, without any lines under it.

reason.description: A few words, like Caring for a family member. Shown as Career break - your words.

explain.description: Optional. One or two sentences the user approved for application questions about a break - no medical or case details. Never on the page; never written without the user.

projects.description: Worth showing but not a job: side projects, class projects, teaching - and clubs, teams or student groups. Dates may be left out; give both or neither.

name.description: The project, or the group exactly as it's called. How a group shows is your call: its full name, a general description you write here, or left off.

role.description: Your part in a club or group: Treasurer, Captain, Member. Prints like a job title.

section.description: The heading it prints under, like Leadership & Activities. Leave it out for Projects.

skills.description: The skills block at the bottom of the page.

items.description: The words listed under that heading.

degree.description: BA, AA, certificate, whatever it was called.

details.description: A minor or honors, as you'd write it: Minor in Mathematics; Dean's List.

start.description: When you started. Never printed; it keeps your time in school from reading as a break between jobs.

end.description: When you finished, or expect to. A date still ahead prints as Expected May 2027.

expected.description: true while you're still earning it: the page says Expected. Once you finish, take it out (or set false).

gpa.description: Exactly as your transcript gives it: 3.62 or 3.62/4.00. Never rounded up. Leave it out if you'd rather not show it.

coursework.description: Courses worth naming for the jobs you want, as your school titles them. Printed as Relevant coursework.

hide_year.description: true leaves the year off the page. Worth it for a degree finished 15 or more years ago; recommended at 20 or more, with your other old years.

certifications.description: Licences and certifications. Leave it as [] if you have none.

hide_year.description: true leaves the date off the page. Worth it for a certification from 15 or more years ago.

languages.description: Languages you speak, one per line, level in brackets: Spanish (Fluent). Levels: Native, Fluent, Professional, Conversational, Basic.

other.description: Anything else worth a heading of its own: volunteer work, awards, a security clearance, publications. Printed exactly as written, after your certifications.

heading.description: The section heading, like Volunteer Work.

lines.description: One line each. Put any dates inside the line.
